![](figures/figureS_rise_factor_matrices/figureS_rise_factor_matrices.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label rise-factor-matrices >}}.
RISE factor matrices.** ({{< panel rise-factor-matrices factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices representing component loadings of conditions and genes; conditions are grouped by ALAD status, then six-month outcome (color strips).
For visualization, genes outside the top 10% by weight in any component are omitted and each component is normalized to its largest absolute loading.

![](figures/figureS_cmp_stability/figureS_cmp_stability.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label cmp-stability >}}.
Collinearity and stability of RISE and CPD components.** ({{< panel cmp-stability cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, receiver, and LR pair factors of any two CPD components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and interquartile range (band) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
({{< panel cmp-stability rise-fms >}}) RISE gene factor and ({{< panel cmp-stability cpd-fms >}}) CPD LR pair factor FMS of each component across leave-one-patient-out jackknife replicates (n = 45), and, right of the dashed line, the aggregate FMS (mean over components) of each jackknife and re-initialization (seed only, n = 100) replicate.
Each replicate's components were matched to the reference's by Hungarian matching.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.

![](figures/figureS_alad_associations/figureS_alad_associations.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label alad-associations >}}.
Association of CPD components, RISE components, and patient covariates with ALAD outcomes.** ({{< panel alad-associations cp-associations >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each CPD component's condition loadings against each ALAD outcome.
\*: q < 0.05, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
({{< panel alad-associations death-weights >}}) CPD component 4 condition loadings by ({{< panel alad-associations death-weights.1 >}}) six-month and ({{< panel alad-associations death-weights.2 >}}) one-year death.
Lines connect samples from the same patient.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
One-way ANOVA F and η^2^, with p Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all outcomes and components.
({{< panel alad-associations rise-associations >}}) As in ({{< panel alad-associations cp-associations >}}), for each RISE component's condition loadings.
({{< panel alad-associations sender-receiver-scatter >}}) Per-cell CPD component 4 sender against receiver weight, with R^2^ across all cells.
({{< panel alad-associations covariates >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each patient covariate against each ALAD outcome, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
\*: p < 0.05, uncorrected.

![](figures/figureS_anova_stability/figureS_anova_stability.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label anova-stability >}}.
Stability of CPD component--outcome associations.** ({{< panel anova-stability effect-size-distributions >}}) ANOVA η^2^ of each CPD component's condition loadings against six-month outcome across leave-one-patient-out jackknife replicates (n = 45), each replicate's components matched to the reference's by Hungarian matching.
Diamonds mark the full-cohort η^2^, filled where q < 0.05.
({{< panel anova-stability significant-fraction >}}) Fraction of jackknife replicates in which each CPD component's association with six-month outcome has q < 0.05.
q: Benjamini--Hochberg corrected p across the five components of each fit.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_rank_selection/figureS_ibd_rank_selection.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-rank-selection >}}.
IBD rank selection.** ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cohort >}}) Schematic of the IBD cohort data\ [@doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) RISE R^2^X across ranks of the fit on all data and, in BiCV, of the fit on the training block (BiCV train) and its prediction of the held-out block (BiCV test); mean ± SD over 10 repeats per rank.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection bicv-test >}}) BiCV test R^2^X from ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) on its own magnified axis.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-r2x-starts >}}) CPD fit R^2^X across ranks: the median (line) and range (band) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
Circle: the elbow of the median curve located by Kneedle\ [@doi:10.1109/ICDCSW.2011.20].
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the LR pair factors of any two CPD components across ranks, for each start (points), colored by whether the start reaches the solution most starts reach at its rank (blue) or another solution (grey).
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-minima >}}) Number of the 10 starts reaching each distinct solution across ranks (starts joined at FMS ≥ 0.95): the solution most starts reach (blue, bottom) and each other solution (grey), colored as in ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}).
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection mode-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, and receiver factors of any two CPD components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and interquartile range (band) over the starts.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices at the selected rank representing component loadings of conditions and genes.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection eigenstate-heatmap >}}) RISE cell-type--eigen-state associations derived from RISE rank-60 projection matrices: mean RISE projection of each cell type's cells onto each eigen-state.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_associations/figureS_ibd_associations.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-associations >}}.
Association of CPD components and covariates with IBD biopsy type.** ({{< panel ibd-associations cp-associations >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each CPD component's condition loadings against each IBD biopsy categorization.
\*: q < 0.05, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all categorizations and components.
({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings >}}) CPD component ({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings.1 >}}) 3 and ({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings.2 >}}) 4 condition loadings by CD inflammation status.
Violins show the distribution of loadings, points show individual biopsies, and ticks mark the median.
One-way ANOVA F and η^2^, with p Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across all categorizations and components.
({{< panel ibd-associations lineage-proportions >}}) Fraction of each biopsy's cells in each coarsely annotated cell type for healthy, CD uninflamed, and CD inflamed samples, on a square-root scale.
Boxes show the median and interquartile range and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the interquartile range.
q: Kruskal--Wallis test across the three groups, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across cell types.
({{< panel ibd-associations covariates >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each biopsy covariate and coarse cell-type fraction against each biopsy categorization, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
\*: p < 0.05, uncorrected.

![](figures/figureS_niches_ibd/figureS_niches_ibd.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label niches-ibd >}}.
CCC-RISE populations against NICHES on IBD.** ({{< panel niches-ibd weight-scatters >}}) Per-cell sender against receiver weight on each CPD component, each relative to its largest value; dashed lines mark the 0.3 cutoff defining each component's sender (S), receiver (R) and both populations.
({{< panel niches-ibd concordance >}}) NICHES concordance of the component 1, 2, 5 and 6 sender (S) and receiver (R) populations (diamonds), as predicted by their fine cell-type labels (circles) and lineages (ticks), and under 1,000 random RISE directions matched for cell type (grey bars, 5th--95th percentiles).
Filled diamonds: q < 0.05; one-sided empirical test against the random directions, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across the 12 populations of the six components.
({{< panel niches-ibd tau-sweep >}}) NICHES concordance of each population minus that predicted by its fine cell-type labels, across population cutoffs (τ); dashed line, no difference; grey line, the 0.3 cutoff used throughout.
Populations of fewer than 10 cells are not drawn.
({{< panel niches-ibd orderings >}}) NICHES concordance of each component 1, 2, 5 and 6 population's number of top-ranked cells under five orderings: a random RISE direction (median of 200, not matched for cell type), the CCC-RISE weight, the positive part of either multiplied by the cell's ligand or receptor expression, and that expression alone; left, each population's NICHES-positive cells and the share of all cells in the cohort that are NICHES-positive.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_rank_selection/figureS_comparator_rank_selection.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-rank-selection >}}.
Rank selection of the label-based comparators.** Each method's own rank selection on coarse and fine labels, ALAD and IBD together; dashed lines mark each cohort's chosen rank, and red circles the Kneedle elbow.
PB, pseudobulk CPD; TC2C, Tensor-cell2cell; STAC, STACCato.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-fit-coarse pb-fit-fine >}}) Pseudobulk CPD fit R^2^X, ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-collinearity-coarse pb-collinearity-fine >}}) largest absolute cosine between the LR pair factors of any two components, and ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-minima-coarse pb-minima-fine >}}) share of starts at the most common minimum, over 10 seeded starts per rank; lines show the median and bands the range over starts.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-elbow-coarse tc2c-elbow-fine >}}) Tensor-cell2cell normalized error (mean and range over 10 random starts), ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-congruence-coarse tc2c-congruence-fine >}}) largest congruence product between two components of a start, and ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-minima-coarse tc2c-minima-fine >}}) share of starts at the most common minimum.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection stac-shares-coarse stac-shares-fine >}}) STACCato eigenvalue share of each component of each mode's unfolding; the dashed line marks the 1% cutoff, and cores are given as sample × LR pair × sender × receiver.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_map/figureS_comparator_map.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-map >}}.
What labels can hold of CCC-RISE components.** ({{< panel comparator-map sender-ceiling >}}) Sender and ({{< panel comparator-map receiver-ceiling >}}) receiver label ceiling of each CCC-RISE component (filled), the share of variance in its per-cell weights held by means over sample and coarse (squares) or fine (circles) label, and the share reproduced by the closest pseudobulk CPD or STACCato column (open).
({{< panel comparator-map alad-columns >}}) ALAD LR columns of each comparator on coarse (C) and fine (F) labels, joined where their cos^2^ is at least 0.09; line width shows cos^2^.
({{< panel comparator-map coarse-map >}}) As {{< fig 5 program-map >}}, on coarse labels.
({{< panel comparator-map ibd-columns >}}) As ({{< panel comparator-map alad-columns >}}), for IBD.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_split/figureS_comparator_split.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-split >}}.
Detection depth, and the mixed IBD components in STACCato.** ({{< panel comparator-split depth-tracking >}}) Depth tracking of every component and LR column: the absolute Spearman correlation across samples between its absolute condition loadings and the samples' detection depth; lines mark medians.
({{< panel comparator-split mixed-pairs >}}) Carrying pairs of IBD components 1 and 5 in the component and in the STACCato columns holding them, as in {{< fig 5 pair-columns >}}.
({{< panel comparator-split mixed-covariation >}}) Co-variation of IBD components 1 and 5 and those columns, as in {{< fig 5 program-covariation >}}.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_covariation/figureS_comparator_covariation.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-covariation >}}.
Co-variation of every method's components.** Components and LR columns above the stricter null in either version of the test, ALAD ({{< panel comparator-covariation pairs-used disjoint >}}) and IBD ({{< panel comparator-covariation ibd-pairs-used ibd-disjoint >}}).
Components and columns with fewer than two carrying pairs, or whose top LR pair carries at least 0.8 of the squared loading, are not shown.
({{< panel comparator-covariation pairs-used >}}, {{< panel comparator-covariation ibd-pairs-used >}}) Number of carrying pairs tested.
({{< panel comparator-covariation all-pairs >}}, {{< panel comparator-covariation ibd-all-pairs >}}) Mean pairwise Spearman correlation across samples ($\bar{\rho}$) of the carrying pairs, over all pairs of LR pairs, and ({{< panel comparator-covariation disjoint >}}, {{< panel comparator-covariation ibd-disjoint >}}) over those sharing no gene.
Ticks show the stricter null, the larger 95th percentile of 2,000 random and 2,000 expression-matched draws; filled points are above it, and crosses mark columns with no gene-disjoint pairs.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_nichenet/figureS_comparator_nichenet.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-nichenet >}}.
NicheNet on CCC-RISE components and comparator LR columns of ALAD.** ({{< panel comparator-nichenet cell-shuffle >}}) Ligand-weighted NicheNet target score of each component and column above its mean over 1,000 rankings with the high and low cells' labels shuffled.
({{< panel comparator-nichenet prior-shuffle >}}) Ligand-weighted percentile of the target scores among the fit's scored ligands, tested against 1,000 copies of the prior with its ligand--target links reassigned.
Filled: q < 0.05, one-sided empirical test, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across the columns of each fit; dashed lines mark no effect.
({{< panel comparator-nichenet closest-columns >}}) Each CCC-RISE component (diamonds) against the comparator LR columns carrying its LR pairs, as in ({{< panel comparator-nichenet cell-shuffle >}}).

![](figures/figureS_comparator_missed/figureS_comparator_missed.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-missed >}}.
Comparator LR columns that no CCC-RISE component carries.** ({{< panel comparator-missed column-contents >}}) The 18 single-pair and mixed-pair comparator LR columns of ALAD (top) and IBD (bottom) and their LR pairs holding at least 5% of the column's squared loading, sized by absolute loading relative to the column's largest; the CCC-RISE row shows each pair's largest such value in any CCC-RISE component.
({{< panel comparator-missed alad-associations >}}) ALAD and ({{< panel comparator-missed ibd-associations >}}) IBD columns' strongest association with an outcome grouping, as effect size (η^2^) against q (one-way ANOVA, Benjamini--Hochberg corrected across the groupings and components of each fit); the dashed line marks q = 0.05.
Boxes list the columns and CCC-RISE components with q < 0.05 in each grouping; H, healthy; CD, Crohn's disease; U and I, CD uninflamed and inflamed.

{{< include figures/tables/alad_outcome_groups.md >}}

**{{< label alad-outcome-groups >}}.
ALAD samples by outcome group.** Number of BAL samples in each ALAD status and six-month outcome group the analyses compare.
Indented groups are subgroups of the group above them.
Two of the 45 patients were sampled twice, in different groups.
